Items.Authors: Wolfgang Gaessler, Santiago Barboza, Frederique Baron, Wolfgang Brandner, Vincent Benz, Paolo Di Marcantonio, René Doyon, Monica Ebert, Adrian Kaminski, Heidi Korhonen, Laura Kreidberg, Werner Laun, Michael Lehmitz, Alessandro Marconi, Paul Mollière, Andreas Quirrenbach, Ralf-Rainer Rohloff, Walter Seifert, Julian Stuermer, Wenli Xu, Alessio Zanutta
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: K-band spectrograph options
Items.Abstract: ANDES is a fiber fed high resolution spectrograph for the ELT, with the goal of providing simultaneous spectra of R~100000 over a wavelength range from 0.35 to 2.4 micron. The project is just finishing Phase-B with the system PDR.  The work on ANDES-K started with Phase-B. The feasibility to extend the baseline wavelength range from 1.8 to 2.4 micron was studied. Fiber throughput losses are higher in K than in other bands, why ANDES-K is placed close to the focal plane, which is putting limits to mass and volume. Due to such constraints, a spectrograph operating at the diffraction limit of the ELT was investigated. PDR of ANDES-K was hold November 2024 and passed successfully. The design is based on few mode fibers. We thoroughly studied the impact of modal noise created by such fibers and how to mitigate. We also developed a single mode fiber alternative. We will summarize our findings, compare existing spectrographs with our approach and finally conclude on the best option of ANDES-K.

Items.Authors: Nicolò Azzaroli, Enrico Pinna, Chiara Selmi, Edoardo Redaelli
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: optical design and analysis of the single conjugate adaptive optics (SCAO) WFS
Items.Abstract: The ANDES (ArmazoNes high Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph) instrument for the ELT includes a complex Single Conjugate Adaptive Optics (SCAO) subsystem for real-time correction of atmospheric wavefront aberrations. This paper describes the SCAO optical design, featuring a common interface arm, a dual-pair Amici Atmospheric Dispersion Corrector, and a high-order pyramid wavefront sensor with auxiliary technical and phasing channels. Sensitivity analyses for component fabrication are detailed, focusing on the pyramid assembly and main optical arm. Key AIV tolerance results quantify how misalignments affect Residual WaveFront Error and PSF/Pupil shifts, defining robust positioning tolerances and confirming compliance with top-level requirements.

Items.Authors: Giorgio Pariani, Luca Oggioni, Ernesto Oliva, Simone Doniselli, Marcello Scalera, Matteo De Magistris, Monica Rainer, Alessio Zanutta, Paolo Di Marcantonio
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: optical design and performance estimation of the fiber routing subsystem
Items.Abstract: The Fiber Routing (FR) subsystem of ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph of the ELT, transfers, scrambles, and reformats the scientific and calibration light from the Front End to the spectrographs, ensuring étendue conservation, illumination stability and high throughput.  We will describe the FR optical design, which followed a process combining first-order modelling, tolerance analysis, and non-sequential simulations. We will show the details of the double scrambler, based on a ball lens, of the pupil slicer, based on a collimator and a micro-lenses array feeding a bundle of small fibers, and of the spectrometer slit, made of a linear array of fibers and micro-lenses. We will also present the full transmission budget —accounting for fiber attenuation, coatings, geometry transitions, and tolerances— across UBV, RIZ, and YJH bands.

Items.Authors: Philippe Bério, Christophe Bailet, Salvador Cuevas, Sébastien Ottogalli, Alain Spang, Mamadou N'Diaye, Andrea Chiavassa, Yan Caujolle, Gaël Chauvin, Omar Gabella, Patrice Martinez, Enrico Pinna, Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli, Julia Seidel, Chiara Selmi, Adrien Simonnin, Paolo Di Marcantonio
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: opto-mechanical design of the coronagraph
Items.Abstract: The ANDES coronagraph is a key subsystem of ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ESO   ELT. Developed in the SCAO sub-system, the coronagraph aims to enhance ANDES’s capability for high-contrast spectroscopy of exoplanets in reflected light, enabling the detection of temperate and rocky exoplanet atmospheres.  The coronagraph optical design is fully refractive. It includes two main arms: a science arm equipped with a Lyot-type coronagraph, and a wavefront sensing arm allowing Non-Common Path Aberration (NCPA) estimation and correction.   The ANDES coronagraph design achieves a contrast level of 3×10⁻³ at 20 mas, compliant with scientific requirements for exoplanet detection. This development represents a major step toward integrating high-contrast imaging and high-resolution spectroscopy on the ELT, bridging the gap between direct imaging and spectral characterization of exoplanets.

Items.Authors: A. Khanbekyan, A. Tozzi, A. Brucalassi, D. Savio, A. Turchi, A. Marconi, M. Rainer, E. Oliva
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: preliminary laboratory results of modal noise mitigation techniques for the fibre injection system of the ANDES-IFU module
Items.Abstract: ANDES high-resolution spectrograph foreseen for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), covering the spectral range from 400 to 1800 nm (with K-band as a goal). It offers two observing modes: a seeing-limited mode, where target light is injected directly into a large fibre, and an IFU mode, where the ELT focal plane is reimaged at different spatial scales onto a microlens array feeding bundles of smaller fibres. In the seeing-limited mode, modal noise is controlled thanks to uniform illumination from natural seeing and fast tip-tilt mirrors. The IFU mode is more exposed to modal noise because the pupil entering each fibre is smaller than the fibre core, especially in the most expanded scale (~7 mas/spaxel), where it is about 18 times smaller. To reduce this, the IFU includes a fast XY piezo stage that moves the pupil during the exposure, improving illumination uniformity. We present preliminary measurements obtained with an ANDES-IFU prototype, testing different XY motions and fibre types.

Items.Authors: Davide Savio, Ernesto Oliva, Matteo Brogi, Lorenzo Pino, Alen Khanbekyan, Anna Brucalassi, Andrea Tozzi, Alessio Turchi, Monica Rainer, Marcello Scalera, Alessandro Marconi, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Alessio Zanutta
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: quantifying the scientific impact of modal noise through laboratory-driven end-to-end simulations
Items.Abstract: Modal noise in multimode fibres is a significant source of systematic error for next-generation fibre-fed spectrographs such as ANDES for the ESO-ELT. We present a study that combines controlled laboratory experiments with end-to-end simulations to quantify its impact on instrument performance. Laboratory measurements under different fibre configurations and illumination conditions provide empirical constraints on the temporal and spectral behaviour of modal noise. These results are used to build an empirical modal noise model integrated into a simulator of ANDES observations. As a case study, we evaluate the effect on exoplanet transmission spectroscopy, showing that modal noise can reduce detection significance and must be mitigated at the hardware level. The study provides quantitative guidance for defining acceptable modal noise levels during ANDES design.

Items.Authors: Philipp Huke, Léa Bonhomme, Christopher Broeg, Isabelle Boisse, Kamalesh Dadi, Michael Debus, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Omar Gabella, Wolfgang Gaessler, Enrico Giro, Jörg Knoche, Viljon Sekseni, Miriam Juliana Brandt, Michael Lehmitz, Jochen Liske, Madhusudan Malve, Piotr Maslowski, Richard McCracken, Christoph Mordasini, Derryck Reid, Ansgar Reiners, Sebastian Schäfer, Mirsad Sarajlic, Joackim Defigueirdo, Cheng Yuk Shan, Alessio Zanutta, Jennifer Zimara, Edoardo Redaelli, Michael Sigwarth, Eike Günther
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: status of the calibration unit design
Items.Abstract: The instrumentation plan for the ELT foresees the ArmazoNes high Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph (ANDES).  All subsystems of the ANDES-project underwent internal subsystems- preliminary design reviews (ssPDR). The systems-level PDR is scheduled for mid 2026 concluding  phase B. Even though the ANDES-spectrograph is designed for maximum intrinsic stability, calibration and thus a  calibration unit (CU) is mandatory. To allow for installation at different places at the ELT (Coudé-room,  intermediate Nasmyth-platform) the CU mirrors the spectrographs design with three independent units. The  design of the individual CU is condensed by now to a high level of detail and ready for the next milestone, the  systems PDR. Here, we show the managerial part of the CU, regarding team and timeline, the engineering design  of one CU (RIZ) and outline the next steps in each element of the CU towards the Final Design Review  and the following Manufacturing, Assembly, Integration and Testing (MAIT) in Europe.

Items.Authors: Michael Weber, Ulrike Lemke, Daniel Sablowski, Katja Poppenhäger, Julián David Alvarado-Gómez, Svend-Marian Bauer, Olga Bellido-Tirado, Joar Brynnel, Edgar Jules Colin, Frank Dionies, Domenico Giannone, Arto Järvinen, Silva Järvinen, Thomas Liebner, Hakan Önel, Jörg Weingrill, Michael Sigwarth, Falk Hoffmann, Markus Roth, Bruno Chazelas, Ian Hughes, Yevgeniy Ivanisenko, Audrey Lanotte, Christophe Lovis, Pedro Morales Sanchez, Michael Sordet, Manuel Amate, Afrodisio Vega Moreno, Jonay I. González Hernández, Ruggero Piazzolla, Wolfgang Gaessler, Michael Lehmitz, Adrian Kaminski, Ingo Stilz, Paolo di Marcantonio
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: the UBV spectrograph module
Items.Abstract: We present the design of the ANDES UBV module, the bluest spectrograph of the ANDES instrument. It is a fiber-fed high resolution, high stability spectrograph, which will be installed on the ELT-Nasmyth platform to minimize blue fibre losses from the focal plane to the spectrograph. In this paper we present the status of development of the spectrograph, its optical design, and auxiliary devices like exposure meter and leveling system, on its way to the final design stage. As stability is the prime design driver, a thermal enclosure is provided to keep temperature of the optical train stable at ambient conditions, the pressure is kept constant inside a vacuum vessel, and the leveling of the instrument is actively controlled. The science, sky background and simultaneous calibration light is fed to the spectrographs via fiber bundles of 66 fibres, which are arranged in a straight row forming the spectrograph slit.

Items.Authors: Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli, Matteo Aliverti, Igor Coretti, Alessio Zanutta
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: thermo-electro-mechanical budget and architecture
Items.Abstract: The ANDES instrument is progressing toward its Preliminary Design Review (PDR), and both the overall architecture and the associated budgets have now reached a consolidated level of definition. This proceeding presents the current system architecture, highlighting the main design drivers and the constraints that shape the instrument’s development.  Emphasis is placed on the thermo–electro–mechanical budget, detailing how thermal stability, electrical routing, structural performance, and subsystem interactions influence the layout and the mechanical concept. The analysis includes the identification of critical interfaces, key performance limitations, and the trade-offs adopted to comply with both scientific and engineering requirements.  This work provides an overview of the rationale behind the architectural choices and outlines the challenges that ANDES faces as it moves toward the next phases of the ELT development cycle.

Items.Authors: P. Picchi, A. Tozzi, A. Brucalassi, A. Khanbekyan, S. D'Auria, V. Baldini, L. Cabona, L. Carbonaro, F. D'Anca, P. di Marcantonio, W. Gaessler, E. Giro, L. Oggioni, G. Pariani, N. Piskunov, M. Porru, M. Rainer, E. Redaelli, M. Riva, D. Savio, M. A. Scalera, A. Zanutta, A. Marconi, E. Oliva, L. Origlia
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrometer for the ELT: AIT/AIV activities on the integral field unit subsystem
Items.Abstract: ANDES is a fibre-fed, high resolution (R=100000) spectrograph of the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), with an observation band between 0.4 and 1.8 micron, with the possibility to extend it toward the U and K bands. ANDES has two observing modes: seeing-limited and Integral Field Unit (IFU), the last one available only in the YJH bands. The IFU mode concluded the sub-system Preliminary Design Review (PDR), and ANDES is progressing toward system level PDR. In this paper, we present the plan and development of the AIT and AIV activities regarding the IFU subsystem, providing details regarding the alignment and the performance verification of the most critical components of the instrument, such as: derotator, Atmospheric Dispersion Corrector (ADC) and the Alignment Check System (ACS) crucial to guarantee the performance of the instrument, especially in the most expanded zoom mode.

Items.Authors: Alessio Turchi, Andrea Tozzi, Alen Khanbekyan, Ernesto Oliva, Davide Savio, Monica Rainer
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrometer for the ELT: statistical description of modal noise in multimode fibers
Items.Abstract: Modal noise in multimode fibers represents a significant challenge for high-precision radial velocity measurements in upcoming spectrographs. ANDES (ArmazoNes high Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph), the first-light high-res spectrograph at the Extremely Large Telescope, has an ambitious goal of ~10 cm/s radial velocity precision, thus mitigating this noise is critical. Modal noise originates from the interference of different propagation modes and translates into wavelength-dependent fluctuations that produce spurious shifts in spectral line positions. This can  mask genuine Doppler signals from exoplanets or stellar activity. In this contribution we present a characterization of modal noise in multimode fibers and investigate if statistical methods can be effective in its description. Our analysis provides new insights into the fundamental behavior of modal noise and its impact on spectroscopic stability, and allows to evaluate potential mitigation techniques.

Items.Authors: Andrea Tozzi, Anna Brucalassi, Alen Khanbekyan, Simone D'Auria, Veronica Baldini, Lorenzo Cabona, Luca Carbonaro, Fabio D'Anca, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Wolfgang Gaessler, Enrico Giro, Luca Oggioni, Giorgio Pariani, Paolo Picchi, Nikolai Piskunov, Matteo Porru, Monica Rainer, Edoardo Redaelli, Marco Riva, Davide Savio, Marcello Scalera, Alessio Zanutta, Alessandro Marconi, Ernesto Oliva, Livia Origlia
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrometer for the ELT: towards the final design of the Integral Field Unit
Items.Abstract: ANDES (ArmazoNes high Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph) is the high-resolution spectrograph for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope, providing unprecedented spectroscopic capabilities in the optical and near-infrared range. The Integral Field Unit (IFU) module has passed its subsystem Preliminary Design Review (PDR), and ANDES is progressing towards system-level PDR. We present the finalized optical design and tolerance analysis results, ensuring required performance across the operational range. The zoom system for spaxel definition, allowing adaptive spatial sampling optimization, is detailed with its implementation strategy. We describe the Alignment Check System (ACS), critical for maintaining optical alignment and performance verification. The mechanical design is presented, including structural architecture and thermal management. Motion control systems enabling IFU reconfiguration are outlined, providing operational flexibility for diverse scientific programs.

Items.Authors: Danielle N. Gurgew, Kirtan P. Dixit, Stephen Bongiorno, Nicholas Thomas, Panini Singam, David Smith
Items.Title: Application of gold release layers for the fabrication of high-angular resolution, replicated full-shell x-ray optics
Items.Abstract: Achieving sub-arcsecond angular resolution with NiCo replicated full-shell optics necessitates improvements to the fabrication process, most notably release from the optical mandrel. Traditionally, NASA Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC) has used a passivation layer to facilitate this step, however, as resolution requirements become tighter, further optimization is required. Thin gold films deposited onto the mandrel before plating have shown promise in reducing errors through initial tests performed on both flat coupons and a small 62mm diameter mandrel. A second, more optically precise mandrel is used in this work to further validate these results by fabricating two shells, one with an optimized Au release layer, and one with the passivation layer. X-ray tests performed at MSFC’s 100m beamline are used to compare performance of the two full-shell optics, further quantifying the Au release layer’s effect on full-shell optical performance.

Items.Authors: Umi Enokidani, Go Murakami, Atsushi Yamazaki, Shingo Kameda, Masato Kagitani, Fuminori Tsuchiya, Ayaka Tadokoro
Items.Title: Application of the high-reflectivity ultraviolet coating for LAPYUTA to gratings
Items.Abstract: We are developing high-reflectivity mirrors to improve the detection efficiency of the focal plane instruments aboard LAPYUTA, a Japanese UV telescope that was selected as one of candidates of JAXA’s M-class mission. For one of LAPYUTA's primary science targets, the atomic oxygen emission line at 130.4 nm, the typical reflectivity of Al + MgF₂ mirrors remains around 85%. Therefore, improving each mirror reflectivity is essential to maintain high detection efficiency. We achieved 90% reflectivity on a flat substrate. Our next step is to apply this coating to gratings. LAPYUTA has two spectrographs: a medium-dispersion spectrograph with spectral resolution R ≈ 6,000, and a high-dispersion spectrograph with R ≈ 40,000. The current coatings reflectivity is 77% at 130 nm, and an absolute diffraction efficiency of 52%. If a coating with 90 % reflectivity can be deposited on the grating, the absolute diffraction efficiency is expected to increase to approximately 60 %.

Items.Authors: Jiahao Zhou, Mengmeng Qian, Wenfei Liu, Hongzhuan Hu, Jianping Wang, Zhigang Liu, Jiaru Chu, Ping Zhang, Zengxiang Zhou
Items.Title: Architecture design and implementation of LAMOST fiber positioning distributed closed-loop control system
Items.Abstract: To meet the control demands of the upcoming large-scale focal plane upgrade for the LAMOST telescope, this research addresses the critical limitations of traditional centralized architectures in scalability and reliability. We propose and implement a novel distributed closed-loop control system for the Fiber Positioning Units. At its core is an innovative hybrid communication framework that effectively integrates high-level messaging with real-time fieldbus networks. Experimental validation confirms that the new system architecture achieves substantial improvements in stability, real-time performance, and scalability compared to the legacy system, providing a robust solution for future ultra-large-scale spectroscopic survey instruments.

Items.Authors: E. Bouzerand, A. M. Glauser, M. Baer, W. Laun, P. Prantl, D. Lesman, T. Huang, Remko Stuik, I. Politopoulos, G. Raskin, M. Salman, G. Jakob
Items.Title: Assembly and testing of the cryostat for ELT/METIS
Items.Abstract: We present the cryostat of the Mid-infrared ELT Imager and Spectrograph (METIS) instrument to be operated at ESO’s Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). The cryostat holds the cold optics and mechanics of the instrument within the required cryo-vacuum environment. The radiation shields of the cryostat are cooled with liquid nitrogen while the cold subsystems are cooled via pulse-tube coolers down to temperatures between 35 K and 70 K. The cold-warm interface is provided with G10 blades that build together with the top part of the cryostat vessel the structural interface to the cold subsystems, the warm support structure, and the warm calibration source. The cryostat has been integrated and tested at ETH where it could be confirmed it fulfills the requirements. We present in this paper the final design, the key design considerations, highlights from the integration and testing phase and final performance.

Items.Authors: Vipin Kumar, Yigit Dallilar, Michael Wiest, Lucas Labadie, Adhirath Deshmukh, Margo Gassmüller, Tarun Kumar Sharma, Dennis Dolkens, Dirk Lesman, Remko Stuik, Adrian Glauser, Bernhard Brandl, Roy van Boekel, Wolfgang Brandner, Christian Staubmeier, Felix Bettonvil
Items.Title: Assembly, integration, and testing of the warm calibration unit for METIS/ELT: optical performance verification and alignment procedures
Items.Abstract: Within the international METIS consortium, the University of Cologne is responsible for the design, manufacturing, integration, and qualification of the Warm Calibration Unit (WCU) subsystem of the instrument. This paper gives an overall view of the AIT phase of the WCU, describing the assembly and alignment operation on its CFRP bench. It focuses on the methods used to bring the subassemblies into their required positions, supporting our AIT workflow. It also provides an overview of the optical performance verification, describing the tests carried out to measure the key optical parameters. The paper also summarizes the opto-mechanical design and optical performance verification of the AIV optics. Finally, we describe the overall strategy for aligning the WCU to the Common For-Optics of the METIS instrument.

Items.Authors: Daniel J. Ahrer, M. Concepción Cárdenas Vázquez, Thomas Bertram, Peter Bizenberger, Armin Huber, Raphaël Pourcelot, Silvia Scheithauer, Horst Steuer
Items.Title: Assembly, integration, and verification of MITESI: an optical testbed for simulating the ELT in the laboratory
Items.Abstract: The MIni elt TElescope SImulator (MITESI) is an optical testbed, operating from λ = 1.50 - 2.42 µm and λ = 3.50 - 4.10 µm, which enables closed loop operations of a wavefront sensor in the laboratory.    In this contribution, we detail the use case and functionality of MITESI and explain how this is achieved on the optical bench by providing an overview of the optical layout. We go on to discuss the assembly and integration of MITESI in the laboratory. We conclude by detailing verification tests carried out to validate and demonstrate the performance of MITESI.

Items.Authors: Miguel Santos, Ana F. Sequeira, Carlos M. Correia
Items.Title: Assessing Reinforcement Learning in XAO Control for PCS
Items.Abstract: The European Extremely Large Telescope (E-ELT) will rely on the Planetary Camera and Spectrograph (PCS) to detect and study exoplanets, demanding an exceptionally fast and precise extreme adaptive optics (XAO) system. This work presents a machine-learning approach designed to ease these real-time control requirements of the PCS.

Items.Authors: Luís Sousa, Carlos Correia, Paulo Garcia
Items.Title: Assessing the astrometric and photometric performance of Starfinder2 in ELT METIS simulated images
Items.Abstract: METIS enables L’-band observations of red objects in stellar clusters and the Galactic Centre, but realistic astrometric and photometric error budgets are lacking. Using a METIS consortium simulation pipeline, ScopeSim, we generated images including field-varying AO PSFs, detector effects, and instrumental characteristics. We apply StarFinder2 to perform advanced source extraction and deblending while accounting for field-dependent variations. Initial tests with SExtractor revealed astrometric errors and a 150 μas precision limit. Starfinder2 is expected to improve these results and provide a more reliable error budget for METIS L’-band imaging.

Items.Authors: Seery Chen, Deborah Lokhorst, Imad Pasha, William Bowman, Steven Janssens, Carter Rhea, Roberto Abraham, Pieter van Dokkum
Items.Title: Assessment of CMOS Detectors for the MOTHRA 1140-lens Array
Items.Abstract: A new telephoto array based on the design of the 48-lens broadband Dragonfly Telephoto Array and the 120-lens  Narrowband Dragonfly Spectral Line Mapper is currently being constructed, with major hardware upgrades and  an order of magnitude increase in lens count. These hardware upgrades will greatly improve observing efficiency,  making it feasible to reach the surface-brightness depths required to directly image the Circumgalactic Medium  and Intergalactic Medium in emission. As part of this upgrade, we take advantage of recent improvements in  CMOS detector technology, and use Atik APX26 and APX60 cameras with Sony IMX571 and IMX455 detectors.  Here, we evaluate the read noise, fixed pattern noise, dark current, bias stability, and performance at varying  gain settings. We compare these measurements with the performance of past cameras used on the Dragonfly  arrays, specifically in the context of low surface brightness imaging with telescope arrays.

Items.Authors: Amirhossein Kermani, Matteo Genoni, Mercello A. Scalera, Marco Riva
Items.Title: AstroMBSE+: extending AstroMBSE methodology based on lessons learned from the CUBES Mission
Items.Abstract: ASTROMBSE methodology is the first MBSE methodology developed specifically for managing astronomical instrument projects. This methodology integrates the primary systems engineering processes, encompassing the management of Requirements, Interfaces, and the Product Breakdown Structure (PBS). In this study, we introduce ASTROMBSE+, an extended version of ASTROMBSE based on lessons learned from the CUBES instrument. Three main refinements are introduced: preserving the PBS code and a general PBS component pool, adding a verification step after the PBS generation phase, and simulating the CUBES maintenance procedures within the model. Overall, ASTROMBSE+ strengthens traceability, supports more reliable configuration control, and extends MBSE support and deployment beyond design into operations, enhancing the full lifecycle management, maintainability, and long-term evolution of a complex astronomical instrument project.

Items.Authors: Danièl Groenewald, Encarni Romero Colmenero, Rosalind Skelton, Alexei Kniazev, Anja Schroeder, Antoine Mahoro, Austun Louw, Christian Hettlage, Enrico Kotze, Lee Townsend, Lisa Crause, Moses Mogotsi, Nhlavutelo Macebele, Phelokazi Dube, Rudi Kuhn, Veronica van Wyk
Items.Title: Astronomy operations of the Southern African Large Telescope (SALT): performance, upgrades, and scientific output
Items.Abstract: SALT is a 10-m class optical telescope located in Sutherland, South Africa. It is owned by an international consortium and operated in fully queue-scheduled mode by the South African Astronomical Observatory, which also manages several other national facilities.    In this paper, we present an updated overview of SALT’s performance, including key metrics such as completion rates, operational efficiency, and scientific output. We also discuss recent strategic developments and instrumentation updates implemented to further enhance the observatory’s performance and scientific impact.

Items.Authors: Changyu Zeng, Teng Xu, Yue Sun, Wei Wei, Chao Liu, Junzhe Huang, Tao Wang, Xuhao Wu, Yonghui Hou, Xiangqun Cui
Items.Title: Auto-alignment and stabilization of the relay optics in long baseline optical interferometer
Items.Abstract: This work presents an auto-alignment system to stabilize long-baseline stellar interferometers against atmospheric and mechanical disturbances. Its two-stage architecture combines slow tip-tilt mirrors (guided by a position sensor) and fast tip-tilt mirrors (controlled by an EMCCD) to correct optical path drift. Testing on a simulated 70-m link under turbulence (single r₀ seeing) demonstrated sub-arcsecond RMS angular stabilization and extended fringe contrast stability to several hours.

Items.Authors: Patricia Van de Walle Suárez, Olivier Absil, Gilles Orban de Xivry, J. Markus Bonse, Robert De Rosa, Valentin Christiaens
Items.Title: Autodifferentiable PSF modeling for the VLT/ERIS vortex coronagraph
Items.Abstract: The Enhanced Resolution Imager and Spectrograph (ERIS) at the VLT is a second-generation mid-infrared imager and spectrograph, and a leading ground-based facility for high-contrast imaging, including a vortex coronagraph mode.    Although the vortex coronagraph provides small inner working angles and high throughput, direct imaging is still limited by residual starlight. To overcome this, we have developed a differentiable optical model of the ERIS vortex coronagraph, optimizing physical parameters via gradient-based methods to accurately reconstruct post-coronagraphic PSFs.    We are now incorporating real-time wavefront telemetry data to model and subtract evolving speckle noise, strengthening the approach for on-sky observations.     We present our framework and early proof-of-concept results using ERIS on-sky data and AO telemetry, demonstrating how model-based post-processing can enhance contrast near bright sources and pave the way for future facilities such as ELT/METIS.

Items.Authors: Enol Matilla-Blanco, Jesús Patrón Recio, Almudena Prieto Escudero, José Leonardo Garces Medina
Items.Title: automatic temperature control loop for cryogenic detectors with Beckhoff
Items.Abstract: Detectors in cryogenics need to be heated and cooled at a specific maximum rate for safety. Also, they need to stay above the optical bench temperature during transitional phases to avoid possible condensation on their surfaces. Because of that, we implemented a complete control loop on a Beckhoff PLC that manages all the changes on setpoints and ramps of the LakeShore 336 (LS336) used to monitor and control the Teledyne Hawaii-2RG detector (H2RG) and the ASIC (Application Specific Integrated Circuit) electronics board of FRIDA instrument (inFRared Imager and Dissector for the Adaptive optics system of the GTC). This control loop also manages failures like helium compressor stops to maintain the detector at a safety temperature point.

Items.Authors: Pierre Bourget, Ivan Cámara Mayorga, Gerardo Smith, Samuel Bonilla, Laurent Pallanca
Items.Title: Automatic tip-tilt adjustment system for the optical metrology delay lines at the VLT: enhancing performance and reducing operational costs
Items.Abstract: At the very heart of the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI), a set of 60-meter-long underground delay lines (DLs) compensate for the optical path difference (OPD) among the astronomical signals received by each telescope. The complex dynamic interplay between DL rails, carriage wheels, and atmospheric factors—such as temperature and humidity—leads to variations and hysteretic behavior in the carriage trajectory along the tunnel. This directly impacts the propagation of the metrology (and astronomical) beams, thus requiring daily rail adjustments and occasionally cumbersome hysteresis/wobble correction of the rails to mitigate its effects. In this manuscript, an automatic tip/tilt correction system acting on the Variable Curvature Mirror (VCM) installed on the DL Cat’s eye, is envisioned to cancel the unwanted effects of carriage trajectory variations. This system will significantly reduce rail adjustment maintenance operations.

Items.Authors: R. Zoufal, R. Ottensamer, F. Kerschbaum, G. Mösenlechner, A. Luntzer, D. Loidolt, M. Mecina, C. Granabetter, S. Kamptisch, M. Güdel, A. Rodriguez-Senin, S. Serrano, T. Rühl, M. Sirianni
Items.Title: Autonomous guide star acquisition for ARRAKIHS
Items.Abstract: The guide star acquisition process for the Arrakihs Fine Guidance System (FGS) and its performance are presented in this contribution. The acquisition autonomously selects guide stars within the field of view, instead of relying on information pre-prepared on ground. The FGS measurements produced by the Arrakihs Common Data Processing Unit’s (CDPU) Instrument Application Software (IASW) are essential for achieving the unprecedented surface brightness targeted by the mission.

Items.Authors: Elisabetta Baracchini, G. Dho, D. Fiorina, S. Piacentini, E. Costa, F. Muleri, P. Soffitta
Items.Title: Background simulations for future x-ray polarimetry missions
Items.Abstract: We will present the preliminary results of a unified simulation campaign aimed at assessing the performance and physics reach of next-generation polarimetric missions. To this end, we studied both an optics-based configuration inspired by the EXPO mission, building on the legacy inaugurated by IXPE, and the newly developed X-POT optical-TPC concept, recently established as a competitive wide-field, collimated hard X-ray polarimeter. Using a Monte Carlo framework validated on IXPE data, we model representative signal and background conditions for each design, evaluating their expected polarimetric response in representative astrophysical scenarios. This joint simulation effort outlines a coherent strategy for future missions combining large-area collimated detectors with high-resolution optics, and establishes a quantitative foundation for optimizing instrument design and defining key science cases.

Items.Authors: Brodi Elwood, P. A. R. Ade, Zeeshan Ahmed, Mandana Amiri, Denis Barkats, Ritoban Basu Thakur, Colin A. Bischoff, Dominic Beck, James J. Items.HTMLTitle: Beam systematics and residual T→P leakage in the BICEP/Keck telescopes
Items.Title: Beam systematics and residual TP leakage in the BICEP/Keck telescopes
Items.Abstract: As CMB polarization experiments—such as BICEP3, BICEP Array (BA), and future BICEP experiments—achieve ever-deeper polarization maps in search of primordial B-modes from inflation, constraining instrumental systematics below statistical uncertainties becomes increasingly challenging. Since the BICEP telescopes are pair-differencing experiments, differential beam response leads to T-to-P leakage, introducing potential systematic bias on the inferred tensor-to-scalar ratio r.  The lowest-order beam-mismatch modes are mitigated through deprojection, though residual undeprojected modes remain. To quantify these residuals, we perform comprehensive in-situ far-field beam measurements of the BICEP receivers. Using beam measurements from BICEP3 (95 GHz) taken in 2016-2019 and 2023; BA1-30/40 in 2020, 2023, and 2024; and BA2-150 in 2023 and 2024, we present analyses of differential beam response and assess the impact of undeprojected residuals on estimates of r for the BK24 data release.

Items.Authors: Benjamin N. Hauptmann, Javier Rico, Giulio Lucchetta, Keerthana R. Lathika, Chiara Perrina, Philipp Azzarello, Juan Boix, David Gascón, Kimberly Keyser
Items.Title: BETA readout electronics for the MiniFIT
Items.Abstract: The scintillating Fiber Tracker (FIT) is a tracking detector for space applications, composed of mats of plastic scintillator fibers and read out by custom silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) arrays. FIT can reconstruct the charge and direction of ionizing particles and enhance the angular resolution of gamma-ray detectors in the MeV to GeV regime.    A custom, low-power ( 5 for single photoelectrons enables charge measurement from Hydrogen to Iron. After characterization of the 16-channel prototype, the 64-channel BETA64 has been completed, characterized, and integrated into a FIT prototype, enabling the measurement of ion tracks. This contribution presents the preliminary results of the BETA64 characterization and the FIT performance in terms of spatial resolution, particle identification, and trigger efficiency.

Items.Authors: Wen-Ping Chen, Ming-Hsin Chang, Yung-Hsin Chang, Ting-Wan Chen, Yi Chou, Daisuke Kinoshita, Chow-Choong Ngeow, Yen-Chen Pan, Anli Tsai, Yair Krongold, Liliana Figueroa, Erica Lugo, Laurence Sabin, Shiang-Yu Wang
Items.Title: Bootstrapping transient astronomy with the Trans-Pacific 2-m Telescope
Items.Abstract: Summary of abstract for display in the program (119 words)    We describe the project to install the Trans-Pacific 2-m telescope facility at the San Pedro Mártir Observatory (SPM) in Mexico, a collaboration between NCU in Taiwan and UNAM in Mexico, together with other international partners. The facility is instrumented, with a simultaneous multiband imager and an efficient spectrograph, to optimize fast characterization of cosmic transient events recognized by, e.g., the LSST or SVOM, in synergy with other telescopes on the same site or in Taiwan. We describe the key parameters of the facility components, such as the telescope, instruments, robotic operations, time allocation and coordinated queue scheduling strategy, alert responses, the status of the project, and forward planning. The telescope is expected to see the first light in 2027/2028.

Items.Authors: Roisin Ryan, Charlotte Feldman, Alejandro Guzmán Cabrera, Lauro Conti, Anna Maskolenko, Paul R. Houghton, Gillian Butcher, Daniel Schuppe, Vadim Burwitz
Items.Title: Building and testing breadboard optics for the soft x-ray imager on the THESEUS mission
Items.Abstract: THESEUS (Transient High Energy Sources and Early Universe Surveyor) is a candidate in ESA’s M7 call, which aims to study high redshift Gamma ray bursts and transient X-ray events. The mission is currently in phase A, with proposed launch in 2037.  The Soft X-ray Imager (SXI) of the mission will consist of two lobster eye modules covering a field of view of 0.5sr. An array of micro-pore optics (MPOs) focuses the image of the soft X-ray sky to an array of CMOS detectors searching for transients in the 0.3-5 keV energy range.  A technology development activity (TDA) was commissioned by ESA to manufacture and perform metrology on frames of slightly varying materials and to charcterize with X-rays MPOs from different manufacturers.  The results, comparison and interpretation of the tests are presented in this work.

Items.Authors: Vincent Deo, Olivier Guyon, Jared Males, Katie Morzinski, Christoph Baranec, Michael Bottom, Mark Chun, Janis Hagelberg, Rebecca Jensen-Clem, Jonas B. Ohland, Nour Skaf, Avinash Surendran
Items.Title: CACAO++: scheduling user experience as the core of adaptive optics RTCs
Items.Abstract: We report on our 3-year effort to redesign and expand the free and open-source Compute And Control for Adaptive Optics (CACAO) RTC toolkit for adaptive optics.  CACAO has long served as the core RTC system for SCExAO and MagAO-X and is now used at multiple facilities (MAPS, AO3k, ULTIMATE,...). CACAO offers a core realtime infrastructure based on high modularity and expandability, and we are continuously broadening its natively available computational features, integrating cutting edge algorithms and hardware accelerations per community needs.    This CACAO++ project targets three goals:  (1) improved usability via documentation, tutorials, visualization tools, simulation interfaces, and a new python configuration layer;  (2) improved collaboration through API refactoring, modern packaging, and CI/CD;  (3) enhanced performance in real-time resource management, HPC interfacing, and multi-node operation.    We invite community feedback/participation in shaping the future of open-source AO RTC

Items.Authors: Adrianah Appleman, Gen Fujimoto, Don Gregory, Kouichi Hagino, Iroha Ichiseki, Miho Katsuragawa, Lux Snyder, Shin'ichiro Takeda, Nicholas Thomas
Items.Title: Calibration of CdTe double-sided strip detectors for the SuperHERO balloon-borne hard x-ray telescope
Items.Abstract: The Super – High Energy Replicated Optics (SuperHERO) balloon-borne telescope is designed to observe in the hard X-ray bandpass with unprecedented angular resolution. Scheduled for a two-day flight in 2029, SuperHERO will use MSFC’s replicated NiCo shell optics to achieve an angular resolution of a 10 arcseconds Half-Power Diameter (HPD) or better. Each of SuperHERO’s seven optical assemblies focuses onto a CdTe Double-sided Strip Detector (CdTe-DSD). Manufactured by iMAGINEX Inc., the CdTe-DSD design is based on the detectors used in the Hard X-ray Imager (HXI) on the Hitomi/Astro-H mission. Each detector consists of a 1 mm thick, 34 × 34 mm block of CdTe, encased between orthogonal cathode and anode strips. The strips are 200 μm wide with a 250 μm pitch, well-matched to SuperHERO’s plate scale. Calibration of all CdTe-DSDs (seven flight units and one spare) is being finalized at MSFC to determine gain, relative quantum efficiency, and spatial resolution.

Items.Authors: Yifan Zhang, Zijian Zhao, Yuxuan Zhu, Yusa Wang, Xiongtao Yang, Can Chen
Items.Title: Calibration of effective area for X-ray focusing mirrors with continuum from the perspective of simulation
Items.Abstract: Currently, driven by the demand for observational sensitivity, the combination of multiple focusing mirror modules is commonly adopted to enhance the effective area of telescope systems. This generates new requirements for ground - based calibration. To address this, we attempt to use detectors operating at high flux, such as SDDs, for the calibration of the effective area of focusing mirrors. Furthermore, we investigate the influence of the detector's energy spectral response on measurements through simulations, and based on these simulation results, we conduct research on corresponding correction methods.

Items.Authors: Ruixuan (Matt) Xie, Adrian K. Sinclair, James Burgoyne, Anthony I. Huber, Scott Chapman
Items.Title: CCAT: a two-octave 1.024-GHz-KID readout featuring an overlap-channel polyphase synthesis filter bank on RFSoC
Items.Abstract: For the 850 GHz module of Prime-Cam on the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope, we present a 1.024 GHz microwave kinetic inductance detector (KID) readout on the Xilinx ZCU111 RFSoC, built around a parallelized overlap-channel polyphase synthesis filter bank and a matching wideband FFT channelizer. The two-octave architecture reads out four independent RF networks, each with 1.024 GHz of instantaneous bandwidth and up to 2048 detectors, and adds on-the-fly control of per-tone frequency, amplitude, and phase—doubling the Gen1 bandwidth and tone capacity while enabling tone tracking. Across DSP simulation, RF loopback, and two KID test chips, Gen2 shows no loss of noise performance relative to the Gen1 baseline and keeps the FFT-only receiver's digital crosstalk bounded; preliminary results suggest detector-noise-limited operation for most channels. FPGA resource and power utilization are reported alongside an assessment of scalability to future large-format KID instruments.

Items.Authors: Stephen C. Parshley, Ronan Higgins
Items.Title: CCAT: final assembly of the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST)
Items.Abstract: The Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST) is a 6-meter diameter, clear aperture, submillimeter (submm) / terahertz (THz) telescope for the CCAT Observatory. The crossed-Dragone optics are modified to correct for coma, resulting in a 7.8° field of view across a roughly 2-meter diameter focal plane. The primary and secondary mirrors are of comparable size and are composed of aluminum panels set on a carbon-fiber-reinforced polymer backup structure. The completed mirrors are mounted inside an Invar tipping structure, which is supported by a steel yoke. The system will deliver a total wavefront error of less than 22 microns at the focal plane. The observatory is located at an exquisite site for submm astronomy at 5600 meters above sea level on Cerro Chajnantor in the Atacama Desert. We present the transport and final assembly of FYST in Chile.

Items.Authors: James R. Burgoyne, Jonah J. Lee, Jordan D. Wheeler, Jason E. Austermann, James A. Beall, Scott C. Chapman, Anthony I. Huber, Johannes Hubmayr, Matthew Koc, Joel Ullom, Anna K. Vaskuri, Michael R. Vissers, Ruixan (Matt) Xie
Items.Title: CCAT: LED mapping the first science array at 850GHz
Items.Abstract: Prime-Cam, one of the first-light instruments for the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope developed by the CCAT Collaboration, will accommodate seven modules, including a central 850 GHz camera. The 850 GHz module uses three arrays of TiN microwave kinetic inductance detectors (KIDs) totaling roughly 38,000 detectors, read out through 12 RF feedlines per array. As part of the characterization pipeline, we perform LED mapping to relate each detector’s measured resonant frequency to its physical position on the wafer. This enables a lithographic trimming step of the KID capacitors that significantly reduces frequency collisions and boosts usable detector yield. We present the design and laboratory characterization of one of the 850 GHz TiN arrays, with emphasis on the implementation, performance, and accuracy of the LED-based mapping procedure.

Items.Authors: Tilak Patel, Anthony Huber, Eve Vavagiakis, Scott Chapman, Michael Niemack
Items.Title: CCAT: optical design of the 410GHz prime-cam module
Items.Abstract: Prime-Cam is a first-generation instrument for the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST), enabling wide-field, multi-frequency observations for cosmology, line-intensity mapping, and dust-rich galaxy studies. We present an optical performance study for a candidate 410 GHz broadband module designed to couple to approximately 21,000 polarisation-sensitive kinetic inductance detectors. The design uses a 3 lens silicon architecture adapted from existing Prime-Cam instrument modules. At 410 GHz, shorter wavelength operation places tighter demands on wavefront quality, beam shape, and detector coupling. Using Zemax OpticStudio and Huygens PSF analysis, we evaluate candidate module positions, compare 350 and 410 GHz performance, and assess field-dependent Strehl ratio, ellipticity, and encircled-energy behaviour. A preliminary tolerancing study, using inverse increment and Monte Carlo methods, tests sensitivity to realistic alignment perturbations.

Items.Authors: Ivan Look, Skyler Padamada, Michael Gouveia
Items.Title: CFHT's tri-annual observatory shutdown and primary mirror cleaning
Items.Abstract: Alongside CFHT’s strides toward upgrading the Building Facility are efforts made toward maintaining the current facility capabilities. One notable event is the planned triannual observatory shutdown, where the main objective is to recoat the telescope’s primary mirror. This paper provides a comprehensive breakdown of events that occurred during CFHT’s 2025 observatory shutdown. The shutdown consists of four main stages: telescope disassembly, primary mirror cleaning/recoating, mirror cell support system inspection, and telescope reassembly. This process occurs over the course of about two weeks and requires help from a variety of disciplines, mainly Operations, Instrumentation, and Software. The telescope disassembly effort may also include disconnecting the telescope’s Cassegrain environment for detailed inspection.

Items.Authors: Deborah Malone, Helawae Kelemu, Ronald Holzlöhner, Timothy Butterley, Angel Otarola, Miska Le Louarn, James Osborn, Nazim Ali Bharmal, Tim Morris
Items.Title: Characterisation and modelling of dome turbulence through temporal covariances: CANARY and VLT analysis
Items.Abstract: This study develops methods for characterising dome turbulence using temporal covariances from open-loop on-sky data collected by the CANARY instrument on the William Herschel Telescope, as well as from detailed simulations of the telescope. These methods are then applied to pseudo open-loop telemetry from the VLT Adaptive Optics Facility to assess generalisation across instruments. Results show the importance of incorporating dome turbulence into adaptive optics simulations for accurate performance prediction.

Items.Authors: Philippa A. Downton, Tom Buggey, Jesper Skottfelt, Douglas Jordan, David Hall
Items.Title: Characterising deep-level silicon defects in EM-CCDs for the Roman space telescope.
Items.Abstract: Direct imaging of exoplanets requires a detector with photon-counting capabilities. Electron-multiplying charge coupled devices (EM-CCDs) enable single photon detection through the addition of a gain register. The Roman space telescope will demonstrate EM-CCDs in orbit and use photon counting to directly image and perform spectroscopy of exoplanets. CCD performance is limited by radiation induced defects in the silicon lattice, which can trap and release charge causing signal loss, which can be detrimental to photon counting. This work employs the "trap-pumping" technique to characterise defects in a Teledyne-e2v CCD201-20 using extended applied phase times to probe a previously unexplored regime of defect emission behaviour by testing at a warmer temperature, highlighting the potential impact of deep-level silicon defects on photon counting performance.

Items.Authors: Jeronimo Calderon Gomez, Frantz Martinache, Nick Cvetojevic, Marc-Antoine Martinod, Vincent Foriel, Nemanja Jovanovic, Pradip Gatkine, David Mary, Roxanne Ligi, Sylvie Robbe-Dubois, Alexis Carlotti, Marc Ferlet, Matteo Pasinetti, Angelie Alagao, Arnaud Striffling, Guillermo Martin
Items.Title: Characterization and on-sky testing of photonic, AWG-based astronomical spectrographs
Items.Abstract: Astrophotonics intends to meet the needs of next-generation instruments at a small footprint, low cost, and high stability, compared to bulk-optics-based alternatives. Much development effort is driven by the stringent requirements of direct detection and characterisation of exoplanets.   Our team works in characterising Arrayed-Waveguide Grating (AWG) chips for photonics-based, high-resolution, near infrared spectroscopy. AWG spectrographs allow to test the feasibility of photonic spectro-interferometers for exoplanet characterization, another step towards fully photonic instruments for astronomy.  We present the current status of our AWG characterisation and a preliminary on-sky qualification campaign at the PAPYRUS AO system. We present the optical bench used, the spectrographs built for on-sky testing, and preliminary results using our high-resolution (H band) AWGs for a set of bright stars, assessing the capabilities of photonic spectroscopy for future compact instruments.

Items.Authors: Enrico Congiu, Fuyan Bian, Carlo F. Manara, Arseniy Kuznetsov, Guido Agapito, Johanna Hartke, Timo Kravtsov, Lisa-Marie Mazzolo, Fabio Rossi, Cédric Plantet, Fernando Selman
Items.Title: Characterization of the MUSE NFM PSF as a function of atmospheric conditions: TipTop calibration
Items.Abstract: The Multi Unit Spectroscopic Explorer (MUSE) achieves exceptional spatial resolution in narrow-field mode (NFM) thanks to its GALACSI adaptive optics (AO) system, yet limitations in point spread function (PSF) characterization still hinder full exploitation of its capabilities. We analyzed a large set of historical standard-star observations to quantify how NFM PSF properties vary with observing conditions, including elevation, seeing, coherence time, wind speed, and wavelength. These empirical relations were used to calibrate TipTop, a fast AO-PSF simulation tool soon to be integrated into the ESO Exposure Time Calculator. Our results confirm that calibration with real on-sky data is essential for accurate PSF modeling. Once implemented, this will provide condition-specific NFM PSF predictions and more reliable signal-to-noise estimates. In the longer term, TipTop may also enable PSF reconstruction for individual observations, significantly improving data analysis and quality control.

Items.Authors: Charles-Antoine Claveau, Trevor T. Nguyen, Hannah Gulick, Jessica R. Lu, Steven V. Beckwith, Kodi Rider
Items.Title: Characterization of the Sony Pregius S IMX530 CMOS detector for high-bandwidth AO and wide-field survey applications
Items.Abstract: Low-cost, high-performance CMOS detectors enable astronomical instruments with many focal-plane channels. Multi-conjugate adaptive optics uses multiple Shack–Hartmann wave-front sensors at high frame rates with sub-pixel centroiding, while space-based and wide-field survey imagers require large-format, small-pixel detectors with low dark current for long integrations; in all cases, low read noise is critical. We present a laboratory characterization of the Sony Pregius S IMX530 CMOS sensor integrated into the QHY530ProII camera. At 10 °C we measure a median dark current of 8.3 e⁻ px⁻¹ ks⁻¹, readout noise of 1.6 e⁻ rms, temporal signal stability of 0.05% rms, ~0.5% non-linearity, inter-pixel capacitance <0.1%, and read-noise correlations ≃0.5%. Astrometric tests yield centroiding precision of 0.012 pixel with systematic errors <0.01 pixel.

Items.Authors: Prakamya Agrawal, SO Collaboration, Kam Arnold
Items.Title: Characterizing optical leakage in the Simons Observatory small aperture telescope
Items.Abstract: The Simons Observatory (SO), located on Cerro Toco in the Atacama Desert in Chile, is a mm-wavelength observatory measuring intensity and polarization anisotropies at angular scales ranging from one arcminute to tens of degrees. The larger scales are the focus of the Small Aperture Telescopes (SATs). We present the findings of a study using observations of the moon with a single SAT observing in the spectral bands centered at 90 and 150 GHz. We investigate signals seen on detectors that are intentionally uncoupled to the telescope optics, searching for spurious optical coupling and electrical crosstalk.

Items.Authors: Félix Sauvourel, Faustine Cantalloube, Philippe Delorme, Stephane Bergeon, Fabien Malbet
Items.Title: Characterizing the wind-driven halo in five years of VLT/SPHERE-IRDIS data
Items.Abstract: Adaptive optics enables high-contrast imaging, but its temporal limitation, namely the servolag error, produces the so-called wind-driven halo (WDH) in the images. The WDH appears in the image as a low-spatial-frequency structure, whose morphology and intensity are governed primarily by high-altitude winds, in particular the jet stream flowing above Paranal. This WDH induces a contrast loss of up to one order of magnitude in the AO corrected-region. Using a new geometrical proxy, we analyse ten years of VLT/SPHERE high-contrast images and measure a WDH occurrence rate of about 70%, far exceeding previous estimates. This result shows that the servolag-induced aberrations in the focal plane image constitute an important limitation in current observations, and requires dedicated mitigation strategies for future high-contrast facilities.

Items.Authors: Xiaoyan Li, Dongge Zhang, Xiaokun Wang, Tingting Liu, Zhengyang Li, Xiangyan Yuan, Xuefei Gong
Items.Title: Chinese Antarctic Survey Telescope for Near Infrared band (AST3-NIR)
Items.Abstract: Dome A, Antarctica, the highest peak of the plateau, offers exceptional advantages for near-infrared astronomical observations, for its unique natural conditions such as extreme dryness, cold temperatures, and long polar nights. While the telescope development faces challenges such as harsh environment, unattended operation, low power consumption requirements, snow and frost on the mirror surface. Chinese Antarctic Survey Telescope for near-infrared band is a wide-field telescope scheduled to get first light in China later in 2026 and planned for installation at Dome A in recent years. This article presents the design specifications of the telescope, the infrared detector, mirror de-icing methods, and the unattended operation software, providing technical pathfinder for future larger-aperture infrared telescopes in Antarctica.

Items.Authors: Airam Salas, Begoña García-Lorenzo, Julio A. Castro-Almazán, Gelys Trancho
Items.Title: CNN-based reanalysis of optical turbulence at the Canary Islands Observatories
Items.Abstract: Atmospheric optical turbulence degrades ground-based observations, and its vertical distribution, given by Cn₂(h), determines key site parameters for high spatial resolution astronomy. The Observatorios de Canarias (OCAN) obtained over 300 nights of Generalized SCIDAR profiles, forming a large turbulence database. We present a CNN-based reanalysis of this dataset, supported by an end-to-end ETL pipeline for efficient preprocessing, mapping, and tensor generation. Turbulence maps are converted into multi-channel tensors and processed through pre-trained CNNs used as frozen feature extractors to obtain deep embeddings. Unsupervised clustering of these embeddings reveals latent atmospheric regimes. This approach offers new insights into turbulence variability at OCAN and showcases a novel large-scale characterization method using modern deep-learning techniques.
